subject: b95J01:B8-B9 — why the counterexample needs an involution, not a 3-cycle

nodes.claim: Why would a 3-cycle not serve as the counterexample in S_3?

For a 3-cycle g in S_3 the least positive exponent with g^k in H is 1 or 3 (identity if g is in H, 3 otherwise), and both divide the index 3, so the conclusion of part (b) would still hold and nothing would be refuted; an involution against the index-3 subgroup gives k = 2 against index 3.
A 3-cycle has order 3, so its powers land in H at exponents that are multiples of 1 or 3.
The subgroup has index 3 in S_3.
The chosen transposition is not in H and squares to the identity, so its least positive exponent is 2.
A candidate element refutes part (b) only if its least exponent does not divide the index; for a 3-cycle the candidates 1 and 3 both divide 3, so it cannot refute.
A 3-cycle satisfies the conclusion of part (b) even with H non-normal, so it is not a counterexample.
